title: Hereditary Genetic Conditions: Counseling and Management
summary: BRCA syndromes, Lynch syndrome, cardiogenomics, and the role of cascade testing in families.

content_blocks.text: Germline pathogenic variants are inherited and present in every cell of the body, including gonads — meaning they can be passed to children. Identifying a hereditary syndrome in one patient unlocks risk management opportunities for the entire family through cascade testing. Several hereditary syndromes have high lifetime penetrance and evidence-based clinical management protocols.

rows: Hereditary Breast & Ovarian Cancer (HBOC)
BRCA1, BRCA2
BRCA1: 72% breast, 44% ovarian; BRCA2: 69% breast, 17% ovarian
Annual MRI + mammogram, risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy, mastectomy option, PARP inhibitors
Lynch Syndrome
MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2, EPCAM
Up to 80% colorectal, 40-60% endometrial, elevated gastric/ovarian/bladder risk
Annual colonoscopy from age 20-25, endometrial biopsy, aspirin chemoprevention (CAPP2)
Familial Hypercholesterolemia (FH)
LDLR, APOB, PCSK9
20x increased MI risk by age 60 without treatment
High-intensity statin + ezetimibe from childhood, PCSK9 inhibitors, LDL apheresis
Hereditary Cardiomyopathy
MYH7, MYBPC3, SCN5A, KCNQ1
Varies by gene — HCM, DCM, Long QT, arrhythmia risk
Annual echo/ECG, ICD consideration, activity restriction, cascade family testing
PTEN Hamartoma Tumor Syndrome (Cowden)
PTEN
85% lifetime breast cancer, thyroid, colorectal, endometrial risk
Annual breast MRI + mammogram from age 30, thyroid US, colonoscopy

content_blocks.text: Cascade Testing: A Family Health Strategy

When a pathogenic variant is identified in a proband, first-degree relatives (parents, siblings, children) have a 50% probability of carrying the same variant. Cascade testing — systematic, variant-specific testing of at-risk relatives — is one of the highest-value interventions in medicine. A single BRCA2 proband diagnosis can trigger testing in 10–20 relatives, identifying carriers who can begin surveillance decades before symptom onset.

content_blocks.body: The ACMG recommends that clinical laboratories report pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in 81 genes (ACMG SF v3.2, 2023) when found incidentally during WES/WGS, regardless of the primary indication. These 'secondary findings' include BRCA1/2, Lynch genes, cardiac channelopathy genes, and FH genes. Patients must consent to receive or not receive secondary findings before testing.
content_blocks.title: ACMG Secondary Findings: Incidental Genomic Disclosure

content_blocks.text: Genetic counselors are essential partners in hereditary syndrome management. Pre-test counseling addresses informed consent, insurance discrimination protections (GINA for health insurance, state laws for life/disability), implications for family members, and psychological impact. Post-test counseling interprets results, facilitates family communication, and connects patients to management resources and research registries.
